$$\frac{\theta}{n} = \frac{2 \pi}{200} \text{ radians}$$

Now, we'll form squares with four of the points as vertices. Each internal angle of a square is $90^\circ$ or $\frac{\pi}{2} \text{ radians}$. Since the diagonal of a square bisects its internal angles, we know that the difference between each internal angle and the angle between two adjacent vertices must be $\frac{\pi}{4} \text{ radians}$.

To form the square, we need to arrange four points such that:

$$
\begin{align*}
\text{Angle between adjacent vertices} &= \frac{\theta}{4n} \\
\text{Diagonal, as the side connecting opposite vertices} &= \sqrt{2}r \\
\text{Difference between internal angles} &= \frac{\pi}{4}
\end{align*}
$$

The first equation represents the angle between adjacent vertices in the square. The second equation is the length of the diagonal for a square of side length $r$, and the third equation is the desired difference between internal angles.

\sqrt{2}r &= \frac{\text{diagonal}}{\sqrt{x}} \\
\theta - \frac{\pi}{2} &= 4\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)
